title: Tuesday, Not Thursday
prerequisites: Can understand a short booking confirmation
observable_outcome: Correct one mistaken booking day and confirm the corrected day and time.
learning_objective: Use Sorry, I meant X, not Y and a short confirmation question to repair one wrong booking detail.

scenario.prompt: You booked Tuesday at 7:30. Reception repeats Thursday at 7:30. Only the day is wrong.
scenario.model: Sorry, I meant Tuesday, not Thursday. So that is Tuesday at 7:30, right?

language.grammar: I meant uses the past form of mean to correct an earlier message. X, not Y contrasts the intended detail with the mistaken one.
language.meaning: Tuesday is the intended day; Thursday is the detail to replace. The confirmation question checks the final shared version.
language.appropriateness: Sorry softens the interruption. A calm voice and stress on Tuesday help signal a repair rather than blame. Sorry - Tuesday, not Thursday is also a suitable shorter repair.
language.time_phrase: So that is Tuesday at 7:30, right? repeats both the repaired day and the unchanged time before the conversation ends.

activities.prompt: Booking card: TUESDAY, 7:30. Reception says Thursday. Which detail needs repair?

options.feedback: Yes. The card and reception disagree about Tuesday versus Thursday; both give 7:30.
No. Both versions say 7:30. Keep the matching detail and repair only the day.
No. Changing 7:30 would create a new mistake. Repair only the evidence that conflicts.

activities.prompt: Which repair clearly replaces the wrong detail?

options.text: Sorry, I meant Tuesday, not Thursday.
options.feedback: Yes. It gives the intended day first, rejects the mistaken day, and stays polite.
This signals disagreement but does not supply the correct day. It can also sound blaming.

options.text: Sorry, I meant Thursday, not Tuesday.
options.feedback: This reverses the evidence. Put the intended detail before not and the mistaken detail after it.

activities.prompt: Reception accepts the correction. Which reply checks the final booking?

options.text: So that is Tuesday at 7:30, right?
options.feedback: Yes. It confirms the repaired day and the unchanged time together.
No. This accepts the mistaken day and conflicts with the booking evidence.
This is unclear. A day does not have one time; repeat the full booking detail instead.

transfer.situation: You asked for room 214. Reception says room 240. The room number is the only mismatch.
transfer.task: Write one polite repair. Then write one question that confirms the final room number.
acceptable_responses: Sorry, I meant room 214, not 240. So that is room 214, right?
Sorry - room 214, not room 240. Just to confirm, it is room 214?
I asked for room 214, not 240. Could you confirm room 214, please?
rubric: The wording is suitable for a service conversation.

review_prompt: Tomorrow, repair this mismatch: you booked Friday at 6:00, but someone repeats Sunday at 6:00.

visual.alt_text: A four-step path: hear Thursday at 7:30, spot that Thursday conflicts with the Tuesday booking, correct Tuesday not Thursday, then confirm Tuesday at 7:30.
visual.text_equivalent: HEAR: Thursday at 7:30 -> SPOT: the booking says Tuesday -> CORRECT: Tuesday, not Thursday -> CONFIRM: Tuesday at 7:30, right?

scenes.title: Evidence
scenes.caption: BOOKING: Tuesday, 7:30
scenes.explanation: Read the booking before you answer. It is the evidence for the intended day and time.

scenes.title: Mismatch
scenes.caption: Reception: Thursday at 7:30.
scenes.explanation: Compare the two details. The time matches, but the day does not.

scenes.title: Repair
scenes.caption: Sorry, I meant Tuesday, not Thursday.
scenes.explanation: Give the intended detail first, then contrast it with the mistaken detail.

scenes.title: Response
scenes.caption: Reception: Tuesday at 7:30. Got it.
scenes.explanation: Reception accepts the repair and repeats the new shared version.

scenes.title: Confirm
scenes.caption: So that is Tuesday at 7:30, right?
scenes.explanation: Check both the repaired day and the unchanged time before ending.

scenes.title: Transfer
scenes.caption: Room 214, not 240.
scenes.explanation: Use the same repair pattern with a different booking detail.

sources.title: Mean
sources.coverage: I mean and I meant can operate as discourse markers that add, clarify, or correct what a speaker says.
sources.limitations: General grammar reference; the booking scenario and repair task are original.

sources.title: You mean
sources.coverage: The expression is used to check or clarify another person's intended meaning.
sources.limitations: Dictionary entry; it does not prescribe one universal service-repair script.
